terms.definition: The ~29.5-day cycle from one New Moon to the next; slightly longer than the Moon's orbital period because Earth also moves around the Sun.
When a body's rotation period exactly matches its orbital period, so it always shows the same face to what it orbits — true of the Moon and Earth.
A phase in which the lit fraction of the Moon visible from Earth is growing, on the way to Full Moon.
A phase in which the lit fraction of the Moon visible from Earth is shrinking, on the way to New Moon.
The fraction of the Moon's visible disc that is lit by the Sun at a given moment, from 0 (New) to 1 (Full).
